kills.name: premarket_range_breakout_v1
kills.reason: Requires NSE pre-market call auction data (09:00-09:08 IST) which is stock-specific and does not exist for NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index. Strategy trades NIFTY 100 constituent stocks and depends on equity-only data (per-stock premarket_high/low from call auction, GIFT Nifty direction filter). Any index-adapted version collapses into the standard ORB thesis, already converted as orb_momentum_v22 and killed four more times for the same reason.

kills.name: index_arb_nifty_components_v1
kills.reason: Pure index arbitrage requiring individual component stock prices (RELIANCE, TCS, HDFCBANK, INFY, ICICIBANK, etc.) and NIFTY futures fair value to compute synthetic_index = sum(component_close[i] * weight[i]) vs nifty_fair basis. Our pipeline only provides the NIFTY index itself (spot_df), option_df, and vix_df — no individual equity feeds, no futures data. Without component prices, the basis signal does not exist. Collapsing to NIFTY index alone eliminates the arbitrage thesis entirely since you cannot measure component-vs-index divergence from index data alone. Explicit kill: requires cross-sectional universe of equity stocks.

kills.name: etf_nav_arbitrage_v1
kills.reason: ETF NAV arbitrage requires (1) real-time iNAV computed from all 50 NIFTY component prices — cross-sectional equity data not in the pipeline, (2) NIFTYBEES ETF price feed — no ETF data in pipeline, (3) order book data for the ETF, and (4) ETF short-selling mechanics. The entire edge is about NIFTYBEES ETF price converging to its indicative NAV — this is not a NIFTY spot direction signal. Stripping away the ETF and iNAV leaves no strategy at all. Explicit kill: depends on ETF-specific data and equity component prices unavailable in the 5-second NIFTY/BANKNIFTY options pipeline.

kills.name: beta_neutral_stat_arb_v1
kills.reason: Pure cross-sectional equity pair trade between TATAMOTORS (high-beta) and HINDUNILVR (low-beta). The entire edge requires individual stock price feeds for both equities to compute rolling per-stock betas vs NIFTY, residual returns for each stock, and an alpha spread between the two stocks. Our pipeline provides only the NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index (spot_df), option chain (option_df), and VIX (vix_df) — no individual equity feeds exist. Without TATAMOTORS and HINDUNILVR prices, the beta computation, alpha spread, and entry signals are impossible. There is no index-equivalent of this strategy: a beta-neutral pair trade between two different equities cannot be replicated from a single index time series. Collapsing to NIFTY vs BANKNIFTY is a completely different strategy and already represents a distinct thesis. Explicit kill: requires cross-sectional universe of equity stocks with individual price feeds.

kills.name: correlation_breakdown_arb_v1
kills.reason: Pure cross-sectional equity pair trade between RELIANCE and ONGC (energy sector). The strategy's entire thesis is monitoring rolling intraday correlation between two specific stocks and trading the spread when correlation breaks down. It requires individual price feeds for both equities, rolling cross-stock correlation, beta-adjusted spread computation, and crude oil as an external filter. Our pipeline provides only the NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index (spot_df), option chain (option_df), and VIX (vix_df) — no individual equity feeds or commodity data exist. Without RELIANCE and ONGC prices, no correlation can be computed. There is no NIFTY-equivalent: RELIANCE-ONGC correlation breakdown does not predict NIFTY index direction at 5-second resolution — the signal is about idiosyncratic equity spread, not broad market direction. Explicit kill: requires cross-sectional universe of equity stocks with individual price feeds.

kills.name: cross_listed_arb_v1
kills.reason: NSE-BSE cross-listing arbitrage for mid-cap equity stocks. The entire thesis is about transient price divergences between the same stock on NSE vs BSE due to differential HFT participation and order flow. This fundamentally requires: (1) a universe of mid-cap stocks dual-listed on both NSE and BSE, (2) order book data from both exchanges simultaneously, (3) simultaneous execution on two different exchanges. NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index is not cross-listed — it trades exclusively on NSE; there is no BSE equivalent of the NIFTY or BANKNIFTY index. Without NSE-BSE dual listing, the entire arbitrage mechanism does not exist. There is no directional NIFTY/BANKNIFTY signal derivable from this thesis. Explicit kill: requires cross-sectional universe of dual-listed equity stocks with per-stock order book data from both exchanges.

kills.name: orb_multi_stock_v1
kills.reason: Pure multi-stock portfolio ORB strategy — trades 5-8 NIFTY 50 constituent stocks simultaneously and derives its entire edge from cross-stock diversification (portfolio win rate ~70% vs individual stock ~52%). Requires per-stock ORB levels, per-stock volume/ATR, correlation matrix of 50 stocks, sector membership caps, per-stock earnings filter, and portfolio beta tracking. Our pipeline provides only the NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index (spot_df), option_df, and vix_df — no individual equity feeds exist. Collapsing to a single NIFTY ORB breakout destroys the diversification thesis entirely and is already converted as orb_momentum_v22 (killed 4+ additional times for the same reason). Explicit kill: requires cross-sectional universe of equity stocks with per-stock price/volume feeds.

kills.name: trade_size_clustering_v1
kills.reason: The entire signal mechanism requires tick-level trade tape — individual transaction records with qty, price, and bid/ask classification — to compute round_lot_ratio (count of round-lot trades / total trades), large_trade_pct (large trades by qty / total qty), and cluster_direction (Lee-Ready signed order flow from round-lot trades). Our pipeline provides only 5-second OHLCV bars (spot_df, option_df, vix_df); no per-trade qty or bid/ask classification is available. Volume in 5-second bars is a pre-aggregated composite — it cannot be decomposed back into individual trade sizes. Even the original strategy explicitly flagged this data dependency as a weakness: 'Tick-level trade data in India is expensive and not available via standard Zerodha API. NSE TBT data feed required.' There is no NIFTY/BANKNIFTY proxy derivable from OHLCV alone that preserves the round-lot institutional clustering thesis — bar-level volume spikes are a far weaker and different signal already covered by existing strategies. Explicit kill: requires tick-level trade tape with per-trade quantity and bid/ask classification, unavailable in the pipeline.

kills.name: nifty_banknifty_spread_v1
kills.reason: Pure NIFTY/BANKNIFTY return-spread pairs trade. The entire signal requires simultaneous data from BOTH indices: nb_spread = banknifty_cumulative_return - nifty_cumulative_return, z-scored over a 45-minute rolling window. Our compute() function receives a single spot_df for one underlying — when trading BANKNIFTY options there is no NIFTY return series available, and vice versa. Without both index data streams, the spread z-score signal is impossible to compute. Additionally, the hold time is 20-60 minutes (10-30x our 15-120 second target horizon) and the mechanism specifically requires extended time windows for z-score reversion to 0. Collapsing to a single-index strategy destroys the pairs-trade thesis entirely, and there is no meaningful NIFTY proxy available within the pipeline (VIX is not a NIFTY return series). Explicit kill: requires two simultaneous index data streams and a 20-60 minute hold horizon incompatible with 5-second options trading.

kills.name: rbi_policy_reaction_v1
kills.reason: Event-calendar strategy that fires exclusively on RBI Monetary Policy Committee announcement days (6 times per year, at 10:00 IST). Three fatal incompatibilities: (1) Requires external event calendar to know it is an RBI day — our pipeline inputs (spot_df, option_df, vix_df) contain no event flags and there is no signal derivable from 5-second OHLCV alone that identifies an RBI day reliably. (2) Requires India 10Y gilt yield data (Phase 4 confirmation: gilt_yield_change < -3 bps) which is not available in the pipeline. (3) Hold horizons are 15-30 min (Phase 3 overshoot fade) and 15-75 min (Phase 4 trend resumption) — these compress to 15-120 seconds only by destroying the thesis entirely: the overshoot-then-trend pattern takes 30-90 minutes to develop and has no 30-second analog. With only 6 trading days/year, the strategy would produce ~12 trades annually — statistically meaningless for any evaluation or optimization. No faster version of the RBI reaction idea exists: the edge is explicitly tied to the multi-phase intraday pattern following a scheduled announcement, which cannot be replicated at 5-second frequency without the event calendar and gilt data.

kills.name: global_cue_reaction_v1
kills.reason: The entire signal requires SGX NIFTY / GIFT NIFTY futures data (sgx_implied_open = last SGX NIFTY price before NSE open) to compute premium_bps = (nifty_open - sgx_implied_open) / sgx_implied_open * 10000 — the excess domestic gap over global cues. Our pipeline provides only NIFTY/BANKNIFTY spot_df (5-second OHLCV), option_df, and vix_df; no GIFT NIFTY futures feed is available. Without the SGX/GIFT NIFTY reference price, there is no signal to compute — the unique edge is specifically the DOMESTIC EXCESS relative to global pricing, not the absolute overnight gap. Stripping away the GIFT NIFTY reference collapses this into a plain gap fade strategy, already converted as gap_fade_reversion_v103. Additionally, the convergence mechanism operates over 10-30 minutes with no 5-second analog — the SGX/NSE NIFTY price alignment is a slow 30-minute institutional arbitrage process.
